sections.h2: Where is Douglas County, Washington, and what towns does it include?
sections.html:
Douglas County lies on the Columbia River in north-central Washington. Waterville is the county seat, but East Wenatchee is the largest settlement and anchors the county's side of the Wenatchee metropolitan area.

The county was created out of Lincoln County on November 28, 1883, and named for the statesman Stephen A. Douglas. The county's Wikipedia entry lists a total area of 1,849 square miles, of which 1,819 is land. Okanogan County lies to the north, Grant to the south, Kittitas to the southwest and Chelan to the west across the river. U.S. 2 and U.S. 97 are the main highways.

Three cities sit inside the county: Bridgeport, East Wenatchee and Rock Island. Mansfield, Waterville and part of Coulee Dam are towns. Unincorporated communities include Beebe, Douglas, Lamoine, Leahy, Orondo, Palisades and Withrow. The city or town a parcel falls in matters when you sell, because the local excise tax rate changes by location.

sections.h2: How many people live in Douglas County, and how many own their homes?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 42,938 residents in Douglas County, up from 38,431 in 2010, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 46,473. About 74.6% of residents lived in urban areas and 25.4% in rural ones.

The county had 17,318 housing units in 2020, of which 11.0% were vacant. Among occupied units, 70.7% were owner-occupied and 29.3% were rented. Roughly 18% of residents were 65 or older, which is why the county's senior exemption matters to many sellers in Douglas County.

sections.h2: Which Douglas County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Douglas County splits the work among the Assessor, the Treasurer, the Auditor and a Board of Equalization. Most offices sit in Waterville on South Rainier Street.

  • Assessor: 213 S Rainier Street, mailing address P.O. Box 387, Waterville. Phone 509-745-8521, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The assessor is Jim Ruud.
  • Treasurer: same building, mailing address P.O. Box 609. Phone 509-745-8525. Felisha L. Rosales is the treasurer. The office also collects excise tax for the state and runs tax foreclosures.
  • Auditor: records deeds. Phone 509-745-8527.
  • Board of Equalization: 203 S Rainier, Waterville, P.O. Box 747. Phone 509-745-8537.

The Treasurer also works under contract for five irrigation districts in the county, so some bills carry irrigation charges alongside the property tax.

sections.h2: How does the Douglas County Assessor value a house?
sections.html:
Washington requires the Assessor to value property at 100% of market value, and Douglas County revalues every property each year. Call 509-745-8521 if your value looks wrong, since the office can fix a record error faster than a formal appeal can.

Tax breaks start with age and income. Residents 61 or older, people retired because of a disability, and veterans with a qualifying disability may be eligible for a senior property tax exemption depending on household income. The Assessor's page links an online screening tool, but the office makes the final call. Agricultural land may qualify for open space treatment, and the Assessor has forms for current use, parcel combinations, destroyed property and address changes.

Property tax pays for cities, the county, fire protection, law enforcement, libraries, parks, roads and schools, which is why a house inside East Wenatchee and one on a rural road near Orondo can have different bills at the same value.

sections.h2: When are Douglas County property taxes due, and how can you pay?
sections.html:
The first half was due April 30, 2026, and the second half October 31, 2026. October 31 fell on a Saturday this year, so ask the Treasurer how a payment dated Monday, November 2 is handled if you have not yet paid.

The Treasurer takes payment through Point and Pay by phone at 866-898-2916 or online through the TaxSifter parcel search. Payments must be processed before 11:59 p.m. Pacific time to count as same day, but they are not posted in real time, so allow two to three business days. Vendor fees are a flat $2.30 for an eCheck, 2.7% for a credit card and 0.95% for a debit card. A live-agent Personal Teller service costs an extra $5.

Under RCW 84.56.020, a missed first half makes the whole year's tax delinquent, and interest is computed monthly. Residential property of four units or fewer pays 9% a year and no penalties, while other property pays 12% plus penalties of 3% and then 8%.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Douglas County assessment?
sections.html:
Douglas County's Board of Equalization is made up of the county commissioners. The county hires an independent hearing examiner to run the hearings and recommend a decision, and the board and clerk operate separately from the Assessor.

File a complete petition by July 1 of the assessment year, or within 30 days of the mailing date printed on your Change of Value Notice, whichever is later. The petition must be filed or postmarked by then.

  • Email: BOE@CO.DOUGLAS.WA.US, received by 5 p.m.
  • Mail: Douglas County Board of Equalization, P.O. Box 747, Waterville, WA 98858.
  • Walk-in only: Public Service Building, 140 19th Street NW, East Wenatchee.

Pay your taxes on time even while an appeal is pending. If the value drops, the county credits your account for the difference. A late filing can sometimes be excused for good cause, and Douglas County provides a waiver of late filing request form for that purpose.

sections.h2: What excise tax applies when you sell a Douglas County house?
sections.html:
Washington's real estate excise tax applies to nearly every sale, and the tax is the seller's responsibility under WAC 458-61A-301. The Douglas County Treasurer collects it as the state's agent, and the sale must be presented within 30 days of the sale date to avoid interest and penalties.

You bring the excise tax affidavit and the deed to the Treasurer first, then to the Auditor for recording. Plan time for it: processing takes 10 to 20 minutes per document, service is first come first served, and the Auditor stops recording at 4 p.m. Title companies and attorneys can file electronically through Simplifile. Courthouse staff cannot draft or review a deed, and mobile or manufactured home sales have special requirements, so call 509-745-8525.

sections.h2: What happens if a Douglas County house is behind on taxes?
sections.html:
The Treasurer has the legal duty to foreclose, seize and sell property for delinquent taxes. Before that point, state law lets the Treasurer accept payment agreements and partial payments, applied to the oldest year first. An income-qualified owner living in the home can ask for interest and penalties to be waived within 60 days of the third anniversary of delinquency if the parcel is facing foreclosure.

Call 509-745-8525 for a payoff figure before you set a closing date. A house in this position can sell, but the tax, interest and any foreclosure costs have to be settled with the Treasurer.

faqs.q: What are the Douglas County property tax due dates?
faqs.a: The first half is due April 30 and the second half October 31. Missing the first half makes the full year's tax delinquent.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Douglas County appeal?
faqs.a: Email BOE@CO.DOUGLAS.WA.US by 5 p.m., mail it to P.O. Box 747, Waterville, or hand it in at the Public Service Building at 140 19th Street NW in East Wenatchee. File by July 1 or within 30 days of the notice, whichever is later.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to pay Douglas County taxes by card?
faqs.a: Credit cards carry a 2.7% vendor fee and debit cards 0.95%. An eCheck is a flat $2.30.

faqs.q: What is the excise tax rate in East Wenatchee?
faqs.a: The local rate is 0.50%. The graduated state rate is added on top, based on the sale price.

faqs.q: Does Douglas County offer a senior property tax exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners 61 or older, people retired due to disability and veterans with a qualifying disability may qualify depending on household income. Call the Assessor at 509-745-8521.
